predecessors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
predecessors.text: Egypt, with Alexandria and Barqa conferred on Ibn Tulun in summer 871

successors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
successors.text: Egypt and Syria, where Abbasid troops 'restored direct caliphal rule' in 905

ledger.x: 898: Aleppo and Qinnasrin are given up.
905: the Abbasids reconquer Egypt and Syria.
905: the Tulunid emirate ends with the deposition of Shayban ibn Ahmad.

wars.name: Tulunid conquest of Syria
wars.outcome: Ibn Tulun took Damascus, Homs, Hama and Aleppo and went on to Tarsus; Antioch resisted ('Governor Sima al-Tawil declined to submit', siege); he returned to Egypt in April 879.

wars.name: Tulunid–Abbasid conflict with al-Muwaffaq
wars.outcome: 'Open conflict between Ibn Tulun and al-Muwaffaq broke out in 875/6' but neither side moved militarily; an assembly at Damascus denounced al-Muwaffaq as a usurper in 883; the treaty of 886 recognized Tulunid authority over Egypt and Syria for thirty years at…

wars.name: Abbasid treaty of 898
wars.outcome: The Tulunids gave up Aleppo, Qinnasrin and 'the capitals'.

wars.name: Abbasid reconquest of Egypt and Syria
wars.outcome: Abbasid troops 'restored direct caliphal rule in Syria and Egypt' in 905 after the Qarmatians swept through the Levant.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; Egypt's Nile valley is firm, the Cyrenaican edge towards Ifriqiya and the Syrian-Jazira edge towards the Euphrates are approximate.
